newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORWEGIAN CROWN UNDER PRESSURE AS ELECTION LOOMS.
newsitem.headline: NORWEGIAN CROWN UNDER PRESSURE AS ELECTION LOOMS.

text.p: The Norwegian crown softened on Wednesday against the mark and the inverse European Currency Unit (ECU) index on foreign selling, dealers said.
At 1050 GMT, the crown stood at 4.1490 against the mark and at 102.31 versus the ECU index compared with 4.1090 and 101.59 at 1400 GMT on Tuesday.
Foreign exchange dealers said sellers came out in the early part of the session but activity had died down around midday.
They attributed the crown's weakness partly to the weaker dollar and a stronger mark but also to the political uncertainty ahead of September's election.
The most recent opinion poll on Monday, carried out for Norsk Gallup for TV2, showed the ruling Labour Party edging slightly ahead but a rise in the number of undecided votes.

The survey also showed the right-wing populist Progress Party picking up support at 22.7 percent of those question, but the three-party centrist block -- previously seen as the main threat to the government of Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland -- marginally dropping back.

"The foreign exchange market has been volatile the past few days. The crown had found support from firmer oil prices and positive inflation figures. However, the crown is pulled to the downside by the uncertain political situation," Eirik Larsen, senior analyst at Den norske Bank Markets (DnB), said.
"The market is swinging back and forth in how it thinks the crown should be priced."
A spokesman for Norway's central bank, Norges Bank, declined to comment on the sudden slide in the currency and whether or not the bank had intervened to stabilise it.
Norges Bank is charged with using monetary policy to hold the crown at a steady exchange rate with a basket of currencies.
